title: Choose Homely's visual world
question: Keep the home-centred direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Lived-in Light
options.lineage: quiet domestic lighting scenes and architectural floor plans
options.thesis: The floor plan is the interface, and live device state visibly changes the home's light and safety atmosphere.
options.viewport: A large two-floor plan fills the screen; device nodes illuminate rooms while safety state stays anchored beneath the plan.
options.risk: Atmosphere cannot weaken status contrast, so every glow is paired with a semantic label and shape.

options.label: Nixie Home Counter
options.lineage: nixie-tube laboratory counters and blackened instrument panels
options.thesis: Every home metric becomes a glowing physical reading with precise mechanical controls.
options.viewport: Orange readings and fixed control banks lead, with the floor plan condensed below.
options.risk: Excellent hardware identity, but it separates residents from the spatial home context.
options.case: Strong product clarity for telemetry, but weaker audience identification than the home-centred direction.

options.label: Saturated Room Set
options.lineage: French pop record sleeves on flat saturated grounds
options.thesis: Each floor owns one confident color field and devices read like a small, closed track list.
options.viewport: One saturated floor fills the frame with four device controls tucked into a tidy edge list.
options.risk: The release-cover grammar is memorable but fuses poorly with safety history and dense configuration.
options.case: High recognition at a glance, but lower product clarity for reports, schedules and safety events.

options.label: Pixel Service Manual
options.lineage: Emigre bitmap specimens and appliance service documentation
options.thesis: Coarse state lettering and fine technical annotations turn the home into a precise living specimen.
options.viewport: A poster-scale floor status sits above dense but ordered device and safety annotations.
options.risk: Distinctive typography risks reducing legibility at large text settings and on dense control screens.
options.case: Clear technical authorship, but weaker accessibility and domestic familiarity than the assigned direction.

canonCard.label: Material smart-home standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional Material 3 dashboard, executed with excellent hierarchy and native behavior.
canonCard.viewport: A top app bar, summary tiles, compact floor plan card and familiar bottom navigation.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable, but less memorable and less spatially specific to Homely.
